intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades across Midlothian, and Borthwickend is no exception. For a small settlement with a strong mix of characterful older homes and newer builds, a well-designed wet room adds genuine daily comfort and long-term property value. Whether you're looking to future-proof your home, create a more accessible bathing space, or simply modernise a tired bathroom, the investment makes real sense here. The key is getting the installation right from the start — proper waterproofing, correct drainage falls, and quality finishes that stand up to daily use for years to come.
localContext: Borthwickend sits in a part of Midlothian where the housing stock tells its own story. Older stone-built properties and period cottages dominate much of the area, and these homes come with their own quirks — uneven floors, thick rubble-filled walls, and older pipework that may need upgrading before any wet room work begins. Modern estate homes in and around Borthwickend tend to have more predictable layouts, but they can still present challenges when it comes to drainage routes and floor structures. One factor worth considering in this area is the moderately hard water supply. Hard water accelerates limescale build-up on shower screens, fittings, and tiled surfaces, so specifying the right materials and finishes — and potentially fitting a water softener — will extend the life of your new wet room considerably. A good installer working in Borthwickend will factor all of this in from the survey stage.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Borthwickend typically follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding what's involved helps you plan realistically. It begins with a detailed survey of the existing bathroom space — the installer will assess floor structure, wall composition, drainage options, and the condition of existing plumbing. In older Borthwickend stone cottages especially, this stage can uncover surprises like timber joists that need reinforcing or drainage that needs rerouting. Once the scope is agreed, the room is stripped back to the bare structure. This is when any remedial work happens — strengthening floors, rerouting pipes, or relocating radiators. The most critical technical stage is the tanking and waterproofing layer, which is applied across the entire floor and up the walls to a sufficient height. Getting this right is non-negotiable — any gaps in the waterproofing membrane will cause damage that's expensive to fix later. Next comes the floor former or screed with the correct fall angle to direct water towards the drain, followed by tiling or other surface finishes. Finally, the shower valve, drain, glass screen if specified, and any additional fixtures are fitted and tested. From start to finish, most Borthwickend wet room installations take between five and ten working days depending on complexity.
pricing: In Borthwickend, wet room installations typically run from around £6,500 to £12,000, reflecting both local labour rates and the nature of the properties here. A straightforward conversion in a modern estate home sits at the lower end, while a project in an older stone-built property — where floor reinforcement, re-routing of pipes, or replastering is needed — will push costs higher. The size of the room, your choice of tiles and fittings, and whether you want underfloor heating added all affect the final figure. Moderately hard water in this area may also prompt some homeowners to factor in water softener installation, which adds to the overall budget but protects the finish long-term. Always get a full itemised quote.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickend and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference on a job like this. Local installers will have worked in period cottages and stone-built properties before — they know what to expect when walls are opened up, and they're not billing you for learning on the job. They'll have established relationships with local suppliers, which helps keep material lead times manageable. They're also easier to get back on-site quickly if any snagging issues arise after completion. For a premium installation in a small community like Borthwickend, that local accountability matters.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickend?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — though it takes more planning than a modern home. Older Borthwickend cottages often have solid floors or timber joists that need assessing before work starts. Walls may need additional preparation before tanking. An experienced installer will survey all of this upfront and price accordingly, so there are no surprises mid-project.

faqs.q: Will hard water affect my new wet room in Borthwickend?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water in this part of Midlothian does mean limescale will build up on fittings and tiles over time. Specifying limescale-resistant finishes, choosing frameless or minimal screens, and using quality descaling products regularly all help. Some Borthwickend homeowners also install a water softener at the same time, which significantly reduces ongoing maintenance.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickend?
faqs.a: Most projects take between five and ten working days, though older properties with structural or plumbing complications can take longer. Your installer should give you a clear timeline after the initial survey. It's worth factoring in that you'll be without use of that bathroom during the work, so planning ahead is sensible if it's your only bathroom.

faqs.q: What's the difference in cost between a basic and a premium wet room in Borthwickend?
faqs.a: The biggest cost variables are the structural condition of the room and your choice of materials and finishes.
